label: Mid/late original-phase inputs of j/t/s/z/k/r/1/m-type tokens in sequences that begin with f/0/o/q/a/d
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (97% of activation mass): never fires at t=0, rarely at t=1, and peaks at orig_idx 4-7 / the last 1-3 tokens before <DEL>. Firing looks like a graded sum of three factors: (1) the current input token: j, t, s, z, k strongest (rate ~0.12-0.18), then r, 1, m; (2) the sequence prefix: a big boost when an early original token (especially the first) is in {f, 0, o, q, a, d}. first_tok=f gives a 3.6x lift, and the same set dominates prev2_tok and next_out; (3) first occurrence of the input token (in_first gives 89% of mass). The top activations (around 0.4) are t/j/z/s/k inputs at positions 3-6 after a prefix like f f 0 or o q q. It does weak residual firing at <DEL> in those same sequences and is nearly silent in the copy phase. No single boolean captures it well. Best F1 is about 0.52 on dev, and mass recall is 0.67. Misses are mostly weaker activations on other letters (e, y, n, b) after an A-prefix. False positives are H tokens where the A-token appeared but the neuron did not cross threshold. This fits an additive, distributed code rather than a crisp rule.
